primary_hypotheses: H1 (T2, primary, Holm): on reworded planted stories (banned and implicit versions), Qwen3-8B neurons detect memes better than both the evasion-aware keyword analyst (keywords:expanded-qwen3-8b) and the lexical classifier (keywords:logreg). Statistic: mean over memes of the twin-AUC difference, intersection-union. Meme-level and plot-level sign flips are both required, and the neutral-meme difference must be above 0. SESOI 0.05 AUC. Falsified if the falsification test (H0: difference >= 0.05) rejects for either rival at both levels. Inconclusive if the audit (85%/95%), or the cross-family fallback (75%/90%), fails or the plain analyst's explicit twin AUC is below 0.75.

H2 (T2, primary, Holm): on reworded planted stories, neurons are non-inferior (margin 0.05 AUC) to emb:qwen3emb-4b, embwin:qwen3emb-4b and emb:e5-large (intersection-union, both sign-flip levels, neutral-subset difference above -0.05). If that holds, superiority is tested as a fixed sequence at H2's Holm level. Falsified if any vector is credibly better by more than 0.05.

H3 (T2, primary, Holm): the 11 DEV concept units are meme-specific in unrelated genres. Statistic: mean over units of [twin AUC on their own meme minus mean twin AUC on every other meme], tested against a permutation of meme labels across units. SESOI 0.05. Falsified if the falsification test (H0: specificity >= 0.05) rejects.

H6 (decision rule outside Holm): on reworded planted stories, no method dominates the neurons. Dominating means a one-sided 95% lower AUC bound at least the neurons' estimate while costing no more per story at 34 memes, with setup amortised over the 816 stories. If some method dominates, the neuron case rests on interpretability. H4 and H5 (lineage, v2) are deferred, keep their numbers and are not tested.

problems.fix: In stage_audit, give each story an opaque id (A01 to A60, in presentation order) and write its numbered sentences and the 5 memes' labels and definitions into human_audit_sample.json, so the page never opens t2_stories.jsonl. analysis._human_audit gets the mapping back by re-running human_audit_sample, which is deterministic. problems.problem: _human_audit (analysis.py lines 3194-3234) counts every row in human_audit.jsonl. A7 says an answer can be changed and the last one counts, so a changed answer is counted twice and n_cells goes up. n_stories, which feeds the 48-story completeness rule, counts any story with at least one answered cell. No test covers a changed answer, an 'unsure' answer or a partial story.
problems.fix: Keep only the last row per (story, meme). Define a story as answered when all 5 of its cells have an answer, and base 'complete' on that. Add unit tests for a changed answer, an unsure answer and a story with only some cells answered. Specify in A7 that the page appends rows, and test audit_page.py's output format before F0.

problems.problem: The audit gate does not decide what the document says it decides. (a) The presence rule for H1-H3 includes the 24 coded cells, but H1-H3 use only banned and implicit versions. A poor coded condition, which is a secondary, can make all three primary claims inconclusive. (b) The absence rule needs at least 95% on 48 control and decoy cells, and an 'unsure' counts as disagreement, so 3 unsure or wrong answers fail H1-H3. Binomially, the gate fails 43% of the time if Mike's true agreement is 95%, and 17% if it is 97%. At 48 stories (about 38 absence cells) only 1 error is allowed. (c) The rule scores cells that Q4 and Q5 have already excluded from the analysis.
problems.fix: Apply the H1-H3 presence rule to banned and implicit cells only (72 cells). Make the coded cells the gate for S-coded. State the absence rule as a maximum error count, or as a one-sided 90% lower bound of at least 0.90, fixed before F0. Leave 'unsure' answers out of the denominator, report them, and fail the audit only if more than 10% of the gating cells are unsure. Compute the rule on cells the per-protocol analysis uses, and report all cells beside it.

problems.problem: Operating points are unequal when scores tie. operating_points takes the (k+1)-th largest control score, so a method with many tied control scores (zero keyword hits) ends up below the 10% FPR. In the synthetic pipeline the realised control FPR was 0.000 for keywords:expanded-qwen3-8b and 0.046 for keywords:tfidf, against 0.096 for every other method. The test only checks FPR <= 0.10, so this passes. O1 then compares neurons at about 10% FPR with the H1 rival at a stricter FPR, which biases O1 towards the neurons. That contradicts 'every method thus works at the same false-positive rate'.
problems.fix: Break ties at the threshold by seeded randomisation, applied the same way to control and planted cells, so each method's expected control FPR is exactly floor(0.1n)/n. Alternatively, add a tiny seeded jitter to every score before thresholding. Change the test to require a realised FPR in [0.08, 0.10] for every method, including a tie-heavy keyword method.

problems.problem: Overlap detection gives up the twin control. Each threshold comes from the controls of all 136 plots, so a method that picks up a meme from the frame of its plots (the frame-leak problem the twin design was built to fix) 'finds' that meme on planted cells even when it is blind to the slot. Its own-plot controls would also fire, but they are only 12 of the 136 controls behind the threshold.
problems.fix: For every method, meme and condition, also report the false-alarm rate on the meme's own-plot control versions at the same threshold. Make the pre-stated detection rule twin-consistent: a planted cell counts as detected only if its score is above the threshold and above its own plot's control score. Keep the current rule as a sensitivity. Add a frame-leak world to test_analysis showing that the leaky method is not credited.

problems.problem: H6 counts neuron variants as rivals. run_cost and dominates compare every by_method entry, and _cost_family maps neurons:<m>:m5, :explicit, :far, :m1ctx, devunit:<m>, length_resid:<m> and the other model's neurons to the same 'neurons' cost family. So if Llama's neurons, or the m5 variant, have a lower bound at or above the Qwen neurons' estimate, H6 reports 'dominated' and the fixed reading says 'the neuron case rests on interpretability', which is wrong. The comparison also uses each method's own set of finite memes rather than a common one.
problems.fix: In run_cost, leave neuron-family entries (neurons:*, devunit:*, length_resid:*) and Claude-based entries out of the set of possible dominators. Compute every method's frontier AUC on the memes the neurons and the method share. Say this in section 9 and test it with a world where Llama's neurons beat Qwen's.

problems.problem: The T2 Benjamini-Hochberg family differs between document and code, and is very large. Section 4 says O1 has four tests and O2 twenty, and that Llama's overlap tests are a replication. overlap_secondaries adds the Llama O1 and O2 tests to the same family. In the synthetic run the family had 200 tests: 82 two-sided pairwise contrasts, 47 S10 tests, the encoder chosen in hindsight, and qwen|llama contrasts in both directions. Easy discoveries, such as neurons against the length floor, loosen the q-values of the prominent secondaries (S-coded, O1, O2). S-coded's power is quoted at alpha 0.05, not at the threshold this family implies.
problems.fix: Pre-register a separate family for the prominent secondaries in Qwen: S-coded (6 tests), O1 (4) and O2 (20), 30 tests in all. Report the Llama versions as replications outside it. Move every pairwise contrast, the per-method S10 tests and the encoder chosen in hindsight to a descriptive or exploratory list. Remove the duplicated qwen|llama contrast. State the exact test count of each family in section 5 and assert it in test_analysis.

problems.problem: The coded condition is not well defined in practice. No check confirms that a code term was introduced, used consistently, and appears only in the coded version: story_checks only bans the listed words, so a coded fill can just be a second banned fill. Q6 salience ratings cover banned, implicit and control fills but not coded ones, so the coded-against-control twins behind S-coded and the coded overlap are not checked for matched stakes. S-coded also has six tests but no rule for its headline claim.
problems.fix: Have the writer JSON return code_terms {meme_id: term}. Add a script check Q2c: the term appears at least twice in the coded slot (at least once if the slot has 1 sentence), in no other version of the plot and nowhere in the frame, and is not on any ban list. Add the coded fills to Q6 (136 more rater sessions) and report coded salience. State that the S-coded headline holds only when all 6 Qwen tests pass in their family; otherwise list the pairs that pass.

problems.problem: Section 6 overstates power for H1 and H2. history/power_sim_v3.py compares the neurons with one rival that has no signal, but H1 takes the larger p over 2 rivals and H2 over 3, and H2 is a non-inferiority test. The figures quoted (0.34 at Holm's first threshold for a 0.056 gap, and so on) are upper bounds for the real tests.
problems.fix: Re-run the simulation with the actual intersection-union tests: 2 rivals for H1 and 3 for H2, with realistic rival signal and correlation, and H2 at its 0.05 margin. Report those figures and label the current numbers as single-rival upper bounds.

files_changed: preregistration/dev_units.json (rebuilt from the committed .gz copies; byte-identical, so effectively unchanged)
fixes: Audit blinding (major): the sample file is now the page's only input (analysis.audit_sample_file). It holds opaque ids A01 to A60 in presentation order, numbered sentences and the memes' labels and definitions. It has no story id, plot, version, writer or genre, and audit_leaks refuses to write a file that would show one. _human_audit maps the ids back by re-running the deterministic sample and checks the file against it. audit_page.py is written now (standard library only, served on 127.0.0.1, reads only that file). test_analysis serves it and checks that neither the file nor the HTML contains a version name, plot id or story id.

Audit counting (major): the page appends rows and only the last row per (story, meme) counts. A story counts as answered only when all 5 of its cells are answered ('unsure' is an answer). Only whole blocks are scored. Tests cover a changed answer, unsure answers, a partial story and incomplete blocks. A7 now states the append-only format, and the format is tested before F0.

Audit gate (major): H1-H3 are gated by presence on the banned and implicit cells plus absence on the control and decoy cells. Coded presence gates S-coded and the coded overlap tests, so a weak coded condition cannot make H1-H3 inconclusive. Each gate passes when the one-sided 90% Clopper-Pearson lower bound reaches its threshold: presence 0.75, which allows up to 10 errors in 60 cells (7 in 48); absence 0.80, which allows up to 7 errors in 60 (5 in 48). Gates use per-protocol cells and report every cell beside them. Unsure answers leave the denominator and are reported, and a gate fails if more than 10% of its cells are unsure. The fallback to the cross-family reader is restated on the same split.

Operating points (major): ties are now broken with seeded keys, applied the same way to control and planted stories, so exactly floor(0.1n) controls are flagged for every method. Realised FPR is now 0.096 for every method, including keywords:expanded (was 0.000) and tfidf (was 0.046). The test requires a realised FPR in [0.08, 0.10] for every method, including a tie-heavy one.

Overlap twin control (major): a planted cell now counts as detected only if the method flags it and does not flag its own plot's control. The threshold-only rule is kept as a sensitivity. The false-alarm rate on each meme's own-plot controls is reported for every method, meme and condition. A frame-leak test world shows the leaky method gets detection 1.00 under the old rule and 0.00 under the new one.

H6 (major): the neurons' own variants (either model's neurons, m1/m5/explicit/far/m1ctx, devunit, length_resid) and Claude-based entries can no longer dominate (analysis.h6_rival). Each rival is compared with the neurons on the memes they share. A test world where Llama's neurons beat Qwen's now gives 'not dominated'; the old rule would have said 'dominated'.

BH families (major): a prominent family of exactly 30 Qwen tests (S-coded 6, O1 4, O2 20); a T2 family of 7 (S8, S9, S10 for the neurons, S11 for the plain analyst, m1 vs m5, neurons vs hidden states, T2-long); a T6 family of 12. Llama tests are replications outside every family. Pairwise contrasts (once per pair, duplicate removed), per-method S10 and S11 and the hindsight encoder are descriptive. Family sizes are stated in section 5 and asserted in the tests.

Coded condition (major): the writer JSON now returns code_terms. New script check Q2c: the term appears at least twice in the slot (once in a 1-sentence slot), never in the frame, in no other version, and on no ban list; a failing coded version is invalid. Coded fills join the Q6 salience ratings (544 rater sessions) with their own repair and a salience-matched sensitivity. Headline rule: all 6 Qwen S-coded tests must reach q<0.05 and the coded gate must pass; otherwise only the passing pairs are listed.

Power (major): history/power_sim_v4.py runs the actual tests: intersection-union over 2 rivals (H1) and 3 rivals (H2), rivals with their own correlated signal, H2 at its 0.05 margin. not_adopted: Absence gate threshold: the review suggested a one-sided 90% lower bound of at least 0.90. At 48-60 cells that allows only 1-2 errors and fails 58-70% of the time when true agreement is 95%, which is worse than the rule it replaces. Adopted 0.80 instead (up to 7 errors in 60, 5 in 48): it fails about 1-3% of the time at 95% and about 70% at 85%. Recorded in section 14.5.

Twin-consistent rule: the review suggested 'above the threshold and above its own control's score'. That rule credits a frame-reading method on about half its cells, which is enough to 'find' about half the memes by chance. Adopted 'flagged, and its own control not flagged', which gives such a method no credit; every method loses the roughly 10% of cells whose control is flagged. Recorded in section 14.5.

Audit strata: instead of the review's example of 4 blocks of 15 (3/3/3/2/2/2), used 10 stories per version in 5 blocks of 12, so that 48 stories is exactly 4 whole blocks. This gives 60 absence cells instead of 48; banned and implicit cells fall from 72 to 60.

On reworded planted stories (banned and implicit versions), the neurons' mean twin AUC over non-dropped memes beats both keywords:expanded-qwen3-8b and keywords:logreg. Statistic: intersection-union p = the larger p of the two rivals; each rival's p is the larger of the meme-level and plot-level sign flips. Holm over H1-H3 (first threshold 0.0167). SESOI 0.05 AUC. The 10 neutral memes must show a positive mean difference. Conditions: the author's audit gates pass (banned+implicit presence lower bound ≥0.75, control+decoy absence lower bound ≥0.80, at most 10% unsure, at least 4 whole blocks), or else the cross-family reader decides; the plain analyst's explicit twin AUC must be ≥0.75. primary_hypotheses.falsifier: Falsified if the one-sided falsification test (H0: difference ≥ 0.05) rejects at alpha 0.05 against either rival, at both the meme level and the plot level, while the Holm test does not reject. If both reject, the verdict is 'supported, below SESOI'. If a check fails or cannot be computed, the verdict is inconclusive; below the minimum (fewer than 100 plots with all six versions valid, or fewer than 28 memes kept) it is 'not run'.

primary_hypotheses.prediction: Decision rule, outside Holm. On reworded planted stories at 34 memes, no rival method dominates the Qwen neurons.
